claims.text: A DNN interatomic potential trained on ab initio liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in high-melting HEAs relative to traditional EAM references.
Traditional EAM references inadequately represent the diverse local atomic environments found in ab initio HEA liquids.
The target materials are multicomponent HEAs in solid and liquid states near their high melting temperatures.
The proposed intervention is to train and deploy a DNN potential using ab initio liquid configurations representative of the high-temperature state.
The method is applicable to refractory W-based HEAs and high-entropy carbides or nitrides.
The applicable temperature range approaches or slightly exceeds 3000 K.
Liquid configurations dominate phase space in the stated temperature range.
A liquid-trained DNN can capture the broad spectrum of local atomic configurations in an ab initio liquid.
Capturing those configurations bridges the configurational spaces of the reference model and the ab initio target.
Training on extensive ab initio liquid data allows the DNN to interpolate among a wide range of atomic configurations.
The broader configurational representation of the DNN reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
Reduced thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will produce faster free-energy convergence.
Reduced thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will produce more accurate free-energy evaluations.
Standard TOR-TILD uses EAM references that struggle to capture the configurational diversity of ab initio liquids.
The improvement will depend on how representative the DNN training data are.
The DNN may be less effective for chemistries or temperatures substantially outside its training domain.
Improvement across HEA compositions is contingent on the DNN remaining robust throughout the targeted composition space.
The magnitude of the expected reduction in path mismatch is not known.
A comparison of DNN and EAM references can test the hypothesis by measuring path mismatch, convergence rate, and free-energy differences over a high-temperature range.
Failure of the DNN reference to measurably improve path mismatch, convergence, or free-energy accuracy relative to the EAM reference would falsify the hypothesis.
